A sensational start
It seems somewhat anachronistic that, on the one
hand, the Haas Formula 1 Team uses Ferrari 067/6
V6 engines, whilst at the same time cooperating
closely with Toyota Gazoo Racing as a technical
partner. The GR logo of Gazoo Racing features
prominently on the cars, and in 2026, TGR from
Toyota will even lend its name to the TGR Haas F1
Team.
It was already evident in 2025 that the collaboration
in simulator development and the exchange of
engineers - spearheaded by team principal Ayao
Komatsu since 2024 - was beginning to bear fruit,
as Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman regularly
finished in the points during the second half of the
season.
Following an impressive 7th place at the 2026
season opener in Australia, Oliver Bearman caused
a real sensation in the Haas VF-26 at the second
Grand Prix in China. Behind the two dominant
Mercedes and the two fast Ferraris, the 21-year-
old Briton crossed the finish line in Shanghai in a
sensational fifth place.
For 20 laps, he had Max Verstappen hot on his
heels and kept his nerve, holding off the former
champion until Verstappen retired on lap 44.
After China, the competition caught up strongly
and Oliver Bearman has only managed to finish in
the points once since then. The sensational early
season was, in any case, a huge motivational boost
for the TGR Haas team.

Whether it is the cherry blossom festival or the
famous tea ceremonies - Japan is still shaped
today by traditions dating back thousands of
years. And despite its chequered history, the
Suzuka 1,000 km has also been preserved as a
traditional event.
Since 1966, this classic endurance race has been
contested by a wide variety of cars: from the
Japanese Super GT and the FIA GT to Group C cars
in the All Japanese Sports Car Championship. And
it was during this era in particular that Porsche
consistently enjoyed success. So it was only
natural to choose three legendary Porsche liveries
for the 911 GT3 R cars competing in the IGTC’s
return to Suzuka in 2025.

The pink pig was a tribute to Porsche’s 917/20 of
Le Mans 1971, the pink-and-white Italiya 911 GT3
to the Kremer-Porsche K3 - which became the first
European team to win at Suzuka in 1981 - and
finally the #7, driven by works drivers Kevin Estre,
Laurens Vanthoor and Patrick Pilet, was adorned
in the retro livery of the New Man Porsche 956, the
Le Mans winner of 1984 and 1985.
Their appearance received huge media coverage,
and the yellow 911 - fielded by Absolute Racing -
came within a hair’s breadth of securing victory.
At the end of the race, it was just 13 seconds
behind the winning BMW M4 GT3 of WRT. By then,
however, the Japanese fans had long since taken
Porsche’s retro cars to their hearts.
